acceptance: `evolve ship --class manual --paths a.go` in a tree that also has an untracked b.go commits a.go only (red: flag provided but not defined)
An attestation bound to a different staged set is refused, as today
`evolve ship --class manual --dry-run --paths a.go` prints a.go as the staged set and changes nothing
fix: Add `--paths p1,p2,…` to `evolve ship --class manual`. It stages exactly those paths (git add -- <paths>, deletions included) and verifies the commit-gate attestation against that staged tree. A path outside the repo, or one that matches nothing, exits 10. `evolve commit-gate run --paths` stages the same set, so the attestation binds it. Without --paths the behaviour is unchanged. --dry-run prints the path set it would stage, with or without --paths. Update skills/commit/SKILL.md and runtime-reference.md's ship classes.

summary: verifyManualConfirm runs `git add -A` before committing (internal/phases/ship/verify.go:181), and the /commit skill stages with `git add -A` (skills/commit/SKILL.md:15) because the manual ship commits the whole tree. The standing rule is to stage explicit paths. A console commit in a tree with unrelated residue therefore either ships the residue or needs a raw `git add <paths>` in a tree that happens to be clean otherwise. `ship --dry-run` runs the checks but does not list what it would stage.
title: `evolve ship --class manual` stages the whole tree; add `--paths` to ship only the named files, and make --dry-run print the staged set (lane part)
